# tny

tny is a C11 TUI + CLI coding-agent harness. It beats vercel-labs/fx on binary size and startup, keeps a Unix-shell UI, and drives four backends through one event loop.

- Site: https://thehumanworks.github.io/tny/
- Source: https://github.com/thehumanworks/tny
- Version: 0.3.0
- Size: 749,264 bytes (~0.71 MiB) stripped (macOS arm64)
- License: see the repository

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/thehumanworks/tny && cd tny && make
make install   # PREFIX=$HOME/.local
```

Or: `curl -fsSL https://thehumanworks.github.io/tny/setup.sh | bash`

Requires a C11 compiler and make. Host binaries (cursor-sdk-bridge, ACP agents) stay external; the Codex CLI is only a login helper.

## Commands

```
tny                         # interactive shell
tny ask [prompt]            # one turn, then exit
tny resume [last|<id>]
tny acp                     # ACP server (native loop only)
tny sessions | session last|<id>
tny providers | models | permissions | workspace | status | doctor | usage
tny cursor COMMAND          # Cursor v1.0.30 management/raw RPC
tny tasks                    # list built-in and discovered task presets
tny task show NAME           # inspect one resolved preset
tny login | logout | setup
tny mcp [list]               # configured MCP servers (source attributed)
```

Leading flags: `--provider cursor|codex|acp|openai` (`--backend` alias), `--cwd`, `--model`, `--task NAME`, `--add-dir`, `--permission-mode ask|auto|yolo` (default yolo), `--json`, `-r`, `-c`. `--task` selects a runtime preset; `--agent CMD` remains the ACP executable option.

`tny ask` stdout is Markdown (or one JSON object with `--json`). Exit 0/1/2/130.

Built-in task presets are `review`, `optimizer`, `document`, and `retro`.
Resolution precedence is workflow-private `TNY_WORKFLOW_TASK_DIR` (when a
workflow explicitly sets it), then project `.tny/tasks/NAME.md`, then user
`~/.tny/tasks/NAME.md`, then the built-in. Markdown files accept only optional
`name:`/`description:` frontmatter and a non-empty UTF-8 body up to 256 KiB;
unsafe names and symlinks are rejected. SSH uses built-ins only. Preset metadata
(name, source, digest) is retained on sessions; resumes restore the snapshot
and reject mismatched selectors, while instruction bodies stay out of status
and session listings.


## Workflows

Source `<prefix>/share/tny/tny-workflows.sh` from Bash or Zsh. Define tasks with `tny_task NAME`, repeat `--after NAME` for dependencies, and run with `tny_workflow_run --jobs N`. Ready roots run in parallel; failed tasks block descendants only; successful direct-dependency outputs feed consumers in declared order. Python and TypeScript expose the same contract through `Workflow` with one native runtime per active task.

## Providers

- openai (default fallback): OpenAI-compatible Responses API (`/v1/responses` SSE; `wire_api: "chat"` selects legacy `/v1/chat/completions`). tny owns tools/MCP/skills/permissions. `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_WIRE_API`.
- cursor: spawn the supported `cursor-sdk-bridge` v1.0.30 and implement its complete public Connect `sdk.v1` HTTP/1.1 contract. Local/cloud agents support CLI images, modes, MCP/subagents, sandbox/review, tool allow/deny, durable runs, artifacts/usage, and authenticated custom-tool/store callbacks. Cursor owns built-in tools and exposes no per-call approval RPC; tny policy applies only to registered custom callbacks. `CURSOR_API_KEY`. wasm is clean unsupported. The private `agent.v1` HTTP/2 route remains rejected.
- codex: the ChatGPT subscription from `codex login` (`$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`) against the Responses-compatible `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` on tny's native loop; tokens auto-refresh. No app-server process.
- acp client: `tny --provider acp --agent CMD -- args`.
- acp server: `tny acp` exposes the native loop only.

## Interactive shell

Unix shell, not an IDE. `/` commands, `@` files, `$` skills. Esc/Ctrl-C interrupt. First paint does not wait on a backend; the selected host is pre-warmed after the banner.

## Cursor management

`tny cursor` provides readable aliases for ping/version/account/models/repositories, create/resume/reload/close/send, run wait/get/list/conversation/observe/cancel, agent get/list/archive/unarchive/delete/messages, artifacts/download, and cloud usage. `delete` requires `--yes`; downloads stream strict base64-decoded bytes with an 8 MiB cap.

`tny cursor rpc SERVICE METHOD [JSON|-] [--yes]` accepts only the 27 public client-to-bridge routes and one bounded JSON object from an argument or stdin. Versioned session pointers retain agent id, run id, durable offset, and local/cloud runtime so dropped Send streams resume through ObserveRun without duplicate events.

Configure trusted protojson under `settings.cursor`: `runtime`, `state_root`, `local_store`, callback enablement, and complete AgentOptions/SendOptions. Project `.tny.json` cannot add Cursor authority. `--ephemeral` strips persistent local-store configuration. The CLI accepts `--image` for Cursor; libtny ABI 1 Cursor conversations and custom tools are supported, but image attachments and management RPCs are not exposed through that ABI.

## Permissions

Default yolo for every provider. ask/auto are opt-ins and enforce the native loop. Cursor built-ins remain host-owned; sensitive registered custom callbacks fail closed unless yolo. Rules live in `~/.tny/settings.json`. Never load repo-local MCP. Foreign project MCP loads only after an explicit global per-harness opt-in.

## tnytty

tnytty is the tiny terminal in the same monorepo: a C11 emulator with a
headless VT core, a pty host, kitty graphics plus bundled `icat`, and a
REST HTTP API so every session is scriptable and shareable.

```
make tnytty                 # tnytty/build/tnytty
tnytty                      # passthrough $SHELL
tnytty run --listen 127.0.0.1:7681 -- htop
tnytty serve [--listen HOST:PORT] [--token T]
tnytty gui                  # macOS native window; clean error elsewhere
tnytty icat FILE|-          # PNG via kitty graphics
```

Loopback API binds need no token. Non-loopback requires `--token` /
`TNYTTY_TOKEN` (or a generated token printed once). Treat the token like
an SSH key.
